clue.text: Happy for one to turn off raw data, but not entirely

indicators.note: to turn asks for the run of letters picked out to be read from right to left
but not entirely says only part of the phrase is used, a run of letters inside it

explanation.surface: Someone cheerful switches off a stream of raw data, though not completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Happy' looks like a mood, but it is one of Snow White's seven dwarfs. 'but not entirely' takes FRAWD from 'off raw data', and 'to turn' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Happy is one of the seven little men in the Snow White tale, so he is an example of the type.

clue.text: Ultimately cooled one's temper in bar

indicators.note: Ultimately points to the final letter of the word cooled that follows

parts.note: one's is I'S, the roman one plus S, written IS
to temper a statement is to moderate or qualify it

explanation.surface: Someone finally calmed down while in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub in the surface but is the verb meaning to exclude.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar someone is to exclude them from taking part, which is a synonym.

clue.text: One piercing cry when heading off

indicators.note: heading off removes the first letter of the word for cry

parts.note: to bawl is to cry loudly

explanation.surface: Someone lets out a piercing cry as they set off.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobbler's tool with a sharp point, used for punching holes in leather.

clue.text: Number keeping a slightly larger number back

indicators.note: keeping means the number holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: four is a number
V is the roman numeral five, just bigger than four

explanation.surface: A figure holds on to a slightly bigger figure that follows it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' sits at the end looking like a reversal signal, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a cause or a candidate is to support or prefer it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Roughly weld an unusual, unknown material for guttering?

parts.note: CA, circa, means roughly or about

indicators.note: unusual tells us the letters of weld an come out in an odd new order

parts.note: X is the algebraic symbol for an unknown

explanation.surface: A welder's rough work on an odd unknown substance used for rain gutters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guttering' suggests roof gutters, but a candle gutters when its flame flickers and its melted wax runs down.
explanation.definitionFit: A guttering candle drips molten wax, so this substance is what does the guttering.

clue.text: Rigid, like traffic bollard that's holding up so long

indicators.note: that's holding means the cone-shaped word contains the other one

parts.note: a traffic cone is cone-shaped, so conic

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, says the word for goodbye is read bottom to top

parts.note: ta-ta is an informal goodbye, like so long

explanation.surface: A traffic bollard standing stiff, holding up the queue for a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so long' looks like a length of time, but it is a farewell, TA-TA.
explanation.definitionFit: A person in a catatonic stupor is stiff and motionless, so the word describes rigidity.

clue.text: Low section of arena — dirt-cheap

indicators.note: section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cheap seat in a stadium, priced at the bottom of the range.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest point of something, as in fortunes reaching their nadir, is a low.

clue.text: Central European's great desire to adopt a Scottish name

indicators.note: to adopt means the word for desire takes in the letter a

parts.note: lust is a strong or great desire
Ian is the Scottish form of John

explanation.surface: A man from central Europe longs to take on a Scottish name.
explanation.definitionFit: Lusatia is a region straddling eastern Germany and western Poland, so its native is central European.

clue.text: One raising game after broadcast quickly turned champion

indicators.note: after places the game-raiser at the end
broadcast tells us the words for quickly turned are taken by how they are spoken

parts.note: whirled means spun round quickly
a beater flushes out game birds for the guns on a shoot

explanation.surface: A sports report on a player who turned a match round quickly to become champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' looks like a match, but it is birds raised on a shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who beats everyone on earth at something is the best, an unbeaten title holder.

clue.text: This Yankee succeeds by right, indeed

parts.note: x means by, as in 3 x 4 dimensions or multiplication
ay, or aye, is an old word for yes or indeed

explanation.surface: An American succeeds by doing right, it is true.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yankee' looks like an American, but it is Y in the radio alphabet, which comes straight after X.
explanation.definitionFit: In the NATO phonetic alphabet, Yankee follows the code word for X, so Yankee succeeds it.

clue.text: Displayed great relish with animated short shown in full

indicators.note: shown in means the trimmed word appears inside the word for full

parts.note: sated means full after eating

indicators.note: short says the word for animated loses its last letter

parts.note: alive means lively or animated

explanation.surface: Someone really enjoyed an animated short film shown complete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'animated short' looks like a cartoon; 'short' drops the E from ALIVE, giving ALIV.
explanation.definitionFit: Drooling at the mouth is a sign of keen appetite, so this shows strong relish.

clue.text: Shy artisan spending every second in the country

indicators.note: spending every second means dropping alternate letters, keeping the first, third and so on

explanation.surface: A timid craftsman spends every other moment out in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Syria is a nation in the Middle East, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Simple time perhaps for children and youth of the fifties

parts.note: an era not for adults, an un-adult era, is a time for children
a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth in Edwardian-style dress

explanation.surface: A simple childhood time and the young people of the 1950s.
explanation.walkthrough: Teddy boys were 1950s British youths in drape jackets and drainpipe trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pure, with nothing added, is plain and simple, as in the unvarnished truth.

clue.text: Unsavoury fancy junk those two eat

indicators.note: junk, as a verb meaning scrap, tells us to break up these letters and rebuild them

explanation.surface: Two people eat junk food, a taste nobody would call wholesome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unsavoury' looks like a judgement, but here it means sweet rather than savoury.
explanation.definitionFit: A liking for sugary things is a fancy for food that is not savoury.

clue.text: Where player can appear fine having abandoned his fear?

indicators.note: having abandoned means the letter for fine is dropped from the actor's fear

parts.note: an actor's fear is stage fright
F is an abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades

explanation.surface: An actor can perform well once he gets over his nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage right is a side of the stage from the actor's view, a place a performer can enter.

clue.text: Obscene gents had to be heard

indicators.note: to be heard says the words for gents had are taken by their sound

parts.note: loo'd, as if gents, a men's toilet or loo, were a verb in the past

explanation.surface: Men had to have their rude remarks overheard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gents' is British for a men's public toilet, a loo.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewd describes crude or indecent behaviour, a synonym for obscene.

clue.text: Popular download having a charge that's hidden?

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
an app is a program you download
rent is a charge for use of property

explanation.surface: A popular downloadable app carries a concealed fee.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not apparent is unseen or concealed, so the word means not evident.

clue.text: A record returned in exchange for one bringing case

indicators.note: returned means the two pieces before it are read in reverse

parts.note: LP is a long-playing record
a tiff is a quarrel, an exchange of words

explanation.surface: Someone sends back an album as a swap for another person's luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks like a suitcase but is a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: The party who brings a lawsuit to court is the claimant, legally named this.

clue.text: One as it were who'd steal doctor's name

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor; the 's makes the next piece belong to him

parts.words: One as it were who'd steal
parts.note: to nick is to steal, so a nicker, as it were, is one who steals

explanation.surface: A thief, so to speak, steals a doctor's reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: Monicker, or moniker, is informal slang for a person's name or nickname.

clue.text: Unexpected weaknesses that held boxer up?

definitions.meaning: a hidden flaw in someone admired, from the statue in Daniel
the boxer Cassius Clay, later Muhammad Ali, stood on his own feet

explanation.surface: A boxer's surprising weak spots that kept him upright.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, from a statue in the Book of Daniel, means a hidden flaw in a revered figure.

clue.text: Singular epithet for men

parts.note: S is an abbreviation for singular in grammar
a tag is a label or epithet

explanation.surface: A unique nickname given to men.
explanation.walkthrough: A stag party, in Britain, is a men-only party before a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Stag describes an event restricted to males, as in a stag night, so it means men-only.

clue.text: Comic way to scoff sandwiches

indicators.note: sandwiches means the word for scoffing holds the other piece between its letters

parts.note: to jeer is to scoff or mock
St is an abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A funny way to wolf down sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoff' looks like eating greedily and 'sandwiches' like food, but they mean mock and enclose.
explanation.definitionFit: A court fool or joker is a comic figure who amuses others.

clue.text: Dread holding broadcast back with light experimentation

indicators.note: holding means the word for dread wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: terror is extreme fear or dread

indicators.note: back means the word for broadcast is read in reverse

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
to light on, or alight, is to land

explanation.surface: Fear of a broadcast being pulled, with some light testing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' looks like the opposite of heavy, but it is the verb meaning to come down, as a bird lights on a branch.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning by trying things and correcting mistakes is a method of experiment.

clue.text: Sign we've lost track of reference collection

indicators.note: we've lost means a piece is removed from the collection's word

parts.note: a library is a collection of books for reference
RY is an abbreviation for railway, a track

explanation.surface: A sign that we've lost our way in the reference books.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scales is a sign of the zodiac, so it is an example of a star sign.

clue.text: Mounting appeal to Anglicans to reflect

indicators.note: Mounting, in a down clue, says the letters climb, so they are read bottom to top

parts.note: oh is an exclamation used in appeal, as in oh please
CE is the Church of England, the Anglican church

explanation.surface: A growing plea to churchgoers to think things over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflect' looks like thinking, but it means to send back a sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeat a sound back, as a cave does, is to reflect it.

clue.text: Fence, perhaps, close to historic castle

indicators.note: close to means the end of the word historic

parts.note: the rook in chess is also called the castle

explanation.surface: A fence standing near an old castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fence' looks like a barrier, but is a receiver of stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A receiver of stolen goods is a criminal, so a fence is an example of one.

clue.text: Sprat eating fat at last, visibly indignant?

indicators.note: eating means the fish's name takes in the letter that follows

parts.note: a brisling is a small fish like a sprat

indicators.note: at last means the final letter of fat

explanation.surface: A little fish finally eating fat, and looking cross about it.
explanation.definitionFit: When angry, an animal's hair stands on end, so showing offence is plain to see.

clue.text: The writer's potential, at first, for mischief

parts.note: the writer's is the setter speaking: I'M, I am

indicators.note: at first means the opening letter of potential

explanation.surface: The author has a talent for causing trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mischief' here is a person: a mischievous child is called a little mischief.
explanation.definitionFit: A naughty little child is a scamp, a mischievous sprite or rascal.

clue.text: Dutch people better off than us?

definitions.meaning: 'my old Dutch' is cockney slang for a wife
how the rich live, as in the saying about seeing how the other lot live

explanation.surface: Are the people of the Netherlands richer than we are?
explanation.definitionFit: A spouse is jokingly a partner, while the wealthy are the other social group.

clue.text: Traveller books place somewhere new to put down roots

definitions.text: place somewhere new to put down roots

parts.note: a rep, or sales representative, is a commercial traveller
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A sales rep books a new place to settle down.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving a plant into a fresh container so its roots can grow is a gardening task.
